Definition: the thigh (from its fleshy softness); by euphemistically the generative parts; figuratively, a shank, flank, side
BiblicalUsage: Yârêk is the thigh, the strong limb of the body, and by extension the side or flank of anything. The souls that came out of the loins of Jacob were seventy, and Ahaz set the brazen altar on the north side of the house.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the body is God's design, and even the thigh of Jacob carries the promise of seventy souls.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
